title: Daan Walk: Jianguo Flower Market to CKS Memorial Hall
excerpt: A 6km weekend walk from the Jianguo flower market through Daan Forest Park and along Yongkang Street to the Chiang Kai-shek Memorial Hall.
content:
This is a weekend walk. It starts in the Jianguo flower market, which only trades on Saturdays, Sundays and some public holidays, crosses Daan Forest Park, the biggest park in central Taipei, stops for food on Yongkang Street and finishes beside the Chiang Kai-shek Memorial Hall. In all it is about 6km, and with time to browse, eat and look around it takes 4 to 6 hours.

Aim to reach the flower market soon after it opens at 09:00, while it's still quiet. By lunchtime the aisles under the flyover are much more crowded.

The Route

To make this your neighbourhood for a few days, our guide to hotels in Daan gives the nearest MRT exit for every hotel on it.

Step-By-Step

  • 1 Start at the north entrance of Jianguo Flower Market, where Ren'ai Road passes under the Jianguo elevated road
    • Zhongxiao Xinsheng (orange and blue lines) and Zhongxiao Fuxing (blue and brown lines) are both roughly ten minutes' walk away
    • If you'd rather start at the south end, Daan Park station on the red line is a couple of minutes west of stop 2 along Xinyi Road
    • The jade market is just north of Ren'ai Road under the same flyover, if you want to see that first
    • Both markets open on Saturdays and Sundays from 09:00 to 18:00 and are free to wander round
  • Walk south through the flower market, which is all under cover, so it works in wet weather too
  • 2 At the Xinyi Road end, have a look at the Artist's Corner stalls, part of the weekend market
    • Older guides describe paintings, ceramics and handicrafts here; we couldn't find a current listing, so treat it as a bonus if it's trading
  • 3 Cross Xinyi Road into Daan Forest Park
    • It's open around the clock and costs nothing to enter
    • Make sure you visit the ecological pond to see the herons, turtles and carp; the island in the middle is where the birds nest
    • There's a nice Louisa café with outdoor seating at the Daan Park station end of the park. Louisa opened a branch at the station in 2022, but we couldn't confirm that it's still trading, so see our Louisa guide or pick up a drink on Xinyi Road before you go in
    • There are no shops inside the park itself
  • Leave by the north-west gate, at the corner of Xinyi Road and Xinsheng South Road, and walk west along Xinyi Road for about five minutes
  • 4 Turn left down Yongkang Street, eat your way along it, then come back north to Dongmen Market, just off Xinyi Road, where the number 4 sits on the map
    • The street and the lanes off it are packed with restaurants, cafés and dessert shops
    • [optional] The original Din Tai Fung, on the corner of Xinyi Road and Yongkang Street, is now takeaway only. For a table, use the Xinsheng branch a short way east on the other side of Xinyi Road, at No. 277, and check the live queue before you join it
    • [optional] Alternatively, try the scallion pancake stand, Toasteria next to Din Tai Fung, or the Yaboo Cafe for something to drink
    • You must also try some shaved ice here, and Smoothie House is a popular choice
    • Take your food to Yongkang Park, halfway down the street, if you want somewhere to sit
  • 5 Continue west along Xinyi Road for about ten minutes to the Chiang Kai-shek Memorial Hall
    • Entry costs nothing, and it opens daily 09:00–18:00; the only closures are the eve and first day of Lunar New Year, 28 February, maintenance days and natural disasters
    • See the museum and galleries at the base of the hall
    • Look at the performance halls, the National Theater and the National Concert Hall, facing each other across the plaza
    • Walk through the gardens and trail
    • Catch both ceremonies. The honour guard drill now takes place outdoors, in front of the main steps, on the hour, nine times a day between 09:00 and 17:00, and is called off in rain. The flag comes down at 17:10 in the cooler half of the year (October–March), 18:10 otherwise (see the Chiang Kai-shek Memorial Hall post for more detail)
  • 6 Cross the square to the Gate of Integrity, then follow the edge of the grounds south to the station's exit 2, served by the red and green MRT lines
  • Optional extra: Jin Feng Braised Pork Rice, one of the most popular local restaurants in Taipei, is a couple of minutes from exit 2 on Roosevelt Road

Where to Eat

  • Yongkang Street is the place for lunch, and most of what's here is within a few minutes of Dongmen exit 5
  • The original Din Tai Fung at No. 194 Xinyi Road only sells takeaway now, from 11:00 on weekdays and 10:30 at weekends, until 20:30. The Xinsheng branch opposite has the dining rooms, and the same hours
  • Tian Jin Onion Pancake is a standing-only stall in Lane 6 off Yongkang Street, and it's open from the morning until late evening
  • Yong Kang Beef Noodles is the sit-down choice for a local lunch, but expect a queue at weekends
  • Toasteria, at No. 200 Xinyi Road, serves Mediterranean food from 09:00 until late, and Yaboo, in Lane 41, opens at midday from Monday to Friday and an hour earlier on Saturdays and Sundays
  • Jin Feng at the end of the walk is cheap and quick, and opens late into the night, but its exact hours vary between sources

Best Time to Go

It has to be a Saturday or a Sunday, since the flower market is empty on weekdays. The market's tourism listing also opens it on some public holidays. The rest of the route works any day, as Daan Forest Park, Yongkang Street and the memorial hall don't close on Mondays.

Start at 09:00, spend the morning in the market and the park, and eat on Yongkang Street around midday. That brings you to the memorial hall in the afternoon. From October to March you can arrive in time for the 17:00 guard drill and then watch the flag come down at 17:10.

The market is covered, but the rest of the route is outdoors, and the guard drill is cancelled when it rains. The memorial hall shuts on typhoon days.

Getting There and Back

Start: Zhongxiao Xinsheng station (orange and blue lines) or Zhongxiao Fuxing station (blue and brown lines), about ten minutes' walk south to the Ren'ai Road end of the market. Daan Park station on the red line is at the Xinyi Road end, if you'd rather skip the north half.

Finish: exit 2 of the CKS Memorial Hall stop, where the red and green lines meet. Exit 5 comes up next to the square if you'd rather leave from there. Our MRT guide covers fares and tickets.

Dongmen station (red and orange lines), halfway along, is useful if you want to break the walk in two: exit 5 brings you up beside Din Tai Fung at the top of Yongkang Street.

Common Questions

How long is the Daan walk?

About 6km, counting the loop inside the park and the wander along Yongkang Street. Most people take between four and six hours, and much of that is spent browsing and eating rather than walking.

Can I do it on a weekday?

You can walk it, but the flower market won't be there. On a weekday, start at Daan Park station and begin with the park instead.

Can I sit down at the original Din Tai Fung?

No. The Xinyi Road branch at the top of Yongkang Street is takeaway only. The Xinsheng branch across the road has seating, and both are first come, first served.

When is the changing of the guard at the memorial hall?

Hourly, with the first drill at 09:00 and the last at 17:00, outdoors in front of the main steps, and not in the rain. It moved out of the statue hall in July 2024.

Is the walk free?

Yes. The markets, the park and the memorial hall are all free, and so are the ceremonies. You'll only spend money on food and anything you buy at the stalls.

Carry On Walking

The Zhongzheng walking route begins at exit 5 of Chiang Kai-shek Memorial Hall station, right where this one finishes. It continues past the East Gate and the Presidential Office to 228 Peace Park.

One stop on the green line takes you to Ximen for the Wanhua heritage walk, which works well as an afternoon and evening on a different day.

If you'd rather head south from Daan Forest Park, the Gongguan walking route starts at Technology Building station, about ten minutes east of the park's south-east corner along Heping East Road.
